Hi Maria — thanks for sending. We reviewed the packet quickly and attached an internal summary + our initial redlines (see SummitCloud_DPA_redline_v1.docx). High level:

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood's default position for hosted inference is that we are a processor of customer data for customer-provided prompts and embeddings; we typically accept processor role in the DPA. If SummitCloud's use includes model fine-tuning with their data, that may change the relationship — please confirm whether training data is in scope for the Order Form.

2) Subprocessor notice: We can accept notice + objection windows but 30 days is aggressive for operational subprocessors. Proposed compromise: 7 days notice + immediate objection right for security-sensitive subprocessors with a temporary suspension pathway while we remediate. Laura / Legal — please confirm if that approach is acceptable.

3) SCCs / TIA: We can sign the SCCs but for certain non-EU hosting (backup or burst capacity), we may need a brief TIA tied to our existing transfer risk mitigations (KMS, encryption in transit & at rest, contractual commitments). Irene — can you confirm whether our existing TIA templating is sufficient or if we should use Summit's Annex?

We have three decision points I'd like legal to weigh in on and give a recommended path so we can hit their 24 Aug steering deadline. Internal note attached: approvals matrix + items slated for escalation.

Next steps proposed:
- Laura: legal redline review on processor language + liability carveout (see inline comments).
- Irene: TIA/hosting confirmation and required evidence list (SOC 2 / KMS).
- Ben: commercial lead — confirm whether we offer the requested liability carveout and any concession budget.

I'll follow up with a consolidated reply to SummitCloud by EOD CET 24 Aug.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 18:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + Order Form + DPA draft for SummitCloud — legal review request

Jonas —

Thanks for flagging. I reviewed the Summit redlines and the proposed SCCs Annex. Summary and recommended edits below (inline comments in the attached PDF):

1) Data Role (Clause 2.1): Accept processor language for inference-only services. If SummitCloud will submit training datasets for model updates we should either (a) preserve processor stance but add explicit scope exclusions for training, or (b) accept controller/processor duality with explicit obligations. Recommendation: keep processor; add an Order Form checkbox for "training enabled" that triggers additional terms.

2) Subprocessor notice: Acceptable compromise is 10 business days notice (not 7) with an objection right and a remediation/suspension path. 30 days is not operationally feasible. We'll draft language to balance procurement's ask and our operational cadence.

3) Liability carveout: We cannot accept a wholesale carveout increasing our cap specifically for EU data incidents. We can offer a targeted concession: limited indemnity for regulatory fines caused by Redwood's gross negligence up to a capped amount (tbd by Ben). This keeps exposure bounded.

4) SCCs vs TIA: We prefer to sign the standard SCCs but attach Redwood's TIA addendum stating our mitigations and subprocessors list. That lets us preserve contractual mitigations and also satisfies their procurement checklist. Irene — if SOC2 + KMS evidence is available, note that in the TIA appendix.

5) Export controls / localization: If they are requiring hard locality for processing (no cross-border burst), that is a commercial ask that requires Dedicated capacity or a special routing SLA. Ben, please confirm if Summit is open to a dedicated deployment add-on.

I'll prepare a tracked-redline DPA with the 10-business-day subprocessor notice, TIA-attachment pattern, and liability concession language. If any of you want live edits, I'm free for a 30-min sync at 09:00 CET Monday.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SummitCloud_DPA_redline_LB_v1.pdf

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form + DPA draft for SummitCloud

Maria — thanks for the packet and patience. Per internal review (see Laura's notes attached) here is our proposed path and timeline: 

1) Roles: Redwood will be Processor for inference-only services. If SummitCloud intends to send any datasets for model training, please flag that on the Order Form and we will treat that as out-of-scope until we agree the training annex.

2) Subprocessors: We cannot accept a 30-day notice window. Proposed language: 10 business days notice + objection right + suspension pathway for security-critical subprocessors. Laura has prepared redline text attached.

3) SCCs/TIA: We will sign the standard SCCs Annex but will accompany it with Redwood's TIA addendum (attached) that lists our mitigations (SOC 2, encryption, KMS controls) and subprocessors. Please confirm whether Summit prefers us to adopt your Annex verbatim or to append our TIA — many customers accept the append approach.

4) Liability: We cannot agree to an uncapped/data-specific uplift. Offer: limited indemnity for regulatory fines due to Redwood's gross negligence, capped at EUR 5M (commercial to confirm). Ben — can you confirm acceptability?

5) Evidence: Irene will provide a SOC 2 summary, current subprocessor roster, and KMS architecture diagram for the TIA appendix. Expect those artifacts by COB Mon, 20 Aug.

If this approach looks acceptable, we'll upload the redlined DPA & a brief memo to the Drive link and loop in Parkwell for any narrow legal negotiation. Our goal is to close commercial terms and get to signature by 31 Aug.

Next steps for you: please confirm (a) training-data scope, (b) whether you need us to adopt your Annex verbatim, and (c) whether your procurement board can accept a limited indemnity cap vs the carveout they proposed.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
